ai.description: Daudin's Sea Snake reaches 1.2 meters. It features a yellowish body with 35–50 black dorsal bands and a laterally compressed tail. The head is small with a distinctively rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis nigrocinctus* is best distinguished by its 40–45 distinct, narrow black bands that completely encircle the body, contrasting with a yellowish-white background.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis nigrocinctus* inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries of the Indian subcontinent, often frequenting mangrove-lined shorelines and silty, turbid sea floors.
ai.behavior: Daudin's sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for bottom-dwelling gobies and other small fish among coral reefs and sandy substrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis nigrocinctus* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a small litter of 3–6 live young. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: Hydrophis nigrocinctus occurs in coastal waters along the eastern and western coasts of the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting shallow marine and estuarine zones.
